newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: OLYMPICS-CAPE TOWN PLEASED BY 2004 GAMES REPORT.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-CAPE TOWN PLEASED BY 2004 GAMES REPORT.

text.p: The head of Cape Town's bid to host the 2004 Olympic Games welcomed an initial IOC report on the city as "highly encouraging" on Friday, saying he was unconcerned at references to South Africa's crime problem.

Chris Ball, chief executive officer of the company in charge of the bid, said Cape Town was probably number four in the running at the moment, but accused Rome of a smear campaign against their African rivals.
"It's really highly encouraging, it's positive, it has no surprises," said Ball, responding to the preliminary report on Cape Town's bid released in Lausanne on Thursday.
"We know we have a limited volume of major facilities. The report doesn't worry about that because it knows we have such a strong government guarantee and we have such good planning.
"The message is coming through that we are well organised and in preparation terms we are strong. We will rank somewhere like fourth if you want to make a weighting on technical issues," Ball said.

Asked if he was confident that Cape Town would be on the shortlist of five contenders to be named on March 7, he said: "Rome is trying to knock us off but all the indications are that we should be there."

Ball said Cape Town had been warned there would be "all sorts of skulduggery in this thing, including disinformation". He said some media reports on the IOC assessment of Cape Town, highlighting a reference to the city's crime problem, were written from "a Rome perspective".
"(They are) glorifying Rome, and hitting Cape Town where Rome is continually trying to hit us, which is on crime.
"If Rome can persuade the world that Cape Town is not safe, then Cape Town can't beat Rome," Ball said.
"The IOC itself understands that crime is not an issue in the Games. The issue is security and Rome has bigger security problems than Cape Town has.
"The report is quite complimentary (on crime). It talks about the work being done and that people understand the issue. It doesn't state any negatives on that," Ball said.
The IOC report said "all levels of authority in the country are aware of and concerned about the serious crime situation the country is facing".

The report said a detailed strategy had been drawn up to reduce crime and increase the level of safety and security. "The full implementation of these plans over the coming years will be a challenge," the report added.
